bull.b: Cloudflare is expanding revenue at a strong pace, indicating sustained demand for its security, performance, and developer platform. Continued growth at this scale can broaden its customer base, increase operating leverage, and reinforce its position as customers consolidate workloads on the edge.

High net retention shows existing customers are increasing their spending, supporting a durable land-and-expand model. Growth in large accounts also improves revenue quality by deepening enterprise relationships and creating more opportunities to cross-sell security, Zero Trust, and developer services.

Positive and improving free cash flow demonstrates that Cloudflare’s subscription-led model is converting significant growth into cash despite GAAP losses. Its substantial liquidity provides resources to fund network investment, product development, and strategic initiatives while supporting ongoing business resilience.

bear.b: Leverage is high for a software company and reduces flexibility if growth slows or funding conditions tighten. Debt obligations can compete with investment in the network and products, while the balance sheet remains more sensitive to execution setbacks than a lightly leveraged recurring-revenue model.

Cloudflare has not yet established durable GAAP profitability, even as revenue scales and non-GAAP results improve. Persistent operating losses limit internally funded growth, make earnings more dependent on adjustments, and leave less evidence that the business can sustain attractive returns through a full operating cycle.

The year-over-year margin decline suggests that rapid traffic and customer growth are not translating fully into gross-profit expansion. If network costs continue rising faster than monetization, Cloudflare may need greater pricing, mix, or infrastructure efficiency gains to preserve the economics of its platform.
